opportunities.title: The Coldcard Bug Was Five Years Old. Nobody Tested For It Anyway.
opportunities.why_now: Galaxy's confirmation of a 5-year-old entropy flaw causing $100M+ across four attack waves is the clearest 'we told you so' security story of the year.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive on the entropy/key-generation flaw with a timeline showing how long the vulnerability sat unexploited — then got mass-exploited in weeks once someone found it, framed as a lesson in why 'audited' isn't 'secure.'

opportunities.title: AI Didn't Just Find the Coldcard Bug Faster — It's Now Draining Wallets Faster Too
opportunities.why_now: Boltz pausing service over AI-assisted attacks and a Bitcoin bridge shutting down because AI found bugs 'too fast' both landed within 24 hours, signaling a phase change in attacker tooling.
opportunities.angle: Trend piece connecting Boltz's pause and the bridge shutdown as the first wave of AI-accelerated exploit discovery outpacing human patch cycles — with a blunt 'your incident response SLA is now measured in hours, not weeks' takeaway.

opportunities.title: 15 Attackers, Same Bug, Same Wallets: What Coldcard's Copycat Wave Says About Disclosure
opportunities.why_now: Galaxy's count of at least 15 independent attackers exploiting the identical flaw shows the vulnerability was effectively public knowledge before users acted.
opportunities.angle: Analysis of the disclosure-to-exploitation gap using the 15-attacker figure as proof that 'quiet patch' strategies fail once a bug is this juicy — recommend concrete self-custody hygiene (firmware version checks, seed rotation) readers can act on today.

opportunities.title: Onchain Panic Is a Feature, Not a Bug: Reading the Coldcard Sell-Off Correctly
opportunities.why_now: The Block/K33 report ties 2026's highest onchain activity to Coldcard panic and floats a 'bottoming pattern' — a security incident is now a market-moving event in real time.
opportunities.angle: Markets-meets-security piece arguing that hardware wallet hacks are becoming macro catalysts, using the K33 bottoming-pattern claim as a hook to explain how security news now trades like a Fed print.

opportunities.title: A Bitcoin Robbery Got Someone Life in Prison — Your Seed Phrase Still Isn't Worth Dying For
opportunities.why_now: The ex-LAPD officer's life sentence for a $350K bitcoin kidnapping, alongside three Missouri men charged over a home-invasion plot, shows physical custody risk is escalating alongside digital exploits.
opportunities.angle: Sharp, voice-forward piece on the rising trend of violent 'wrench attacks' tied to visible self-custody wealth, using both cases as proof that opsec now includes not posting your bag size — pairs security advice with true-crime pacing.
